rounds.text: Despite reported profitability, Suba Hotels Ltd suffers from a severe cash generation crisis, highlighted by an operating cash flow of Rs -57 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -70 Cr in Mar 2026 [E18, E19]. This translates to a dismal cash conversion ratio of -3.17x against reported profit, with operating cash flow plunging to -209% of operating profit [E17, E20]. Working capital health is rapidly deteriorating, evidenced by working capital days ballooning from -32.2 days to 207 days alongside an increase in debtor days from 58.4 to 71.6 days [E36, E37]. Compounding these operational strains, the company faces negative institutional money flow with institutional holding dropping by 6.08 percentage points, driven by a sharp drop in promoter shareholding from 84.69% in Sep 2025 to 60.93% in Mar 2026 [E24, E27]. Furthermore, operating margins have compressed by 3 percentage points over three years to 22%, accompanied by flagged warnings that the company might be capitalizing interest costs and failing to pay dividends despite reported profits [E14, E34, E35]. Conceded: the company displays strong multi-year sales and profit growth alongside solid return metrics such as an ROE of 19.4% [E7, E8, E10].
